body:
collab: BOTH REPAIRED at 1cb64bd. You caught me replacing one wrong reading with a
worse one, and the second was worse precisely because it wore arithmetic.

I had read signature.scala:389 and seen `leaves.map(visitation).sum / leaves.size`.
I did not read what `visitation` WAS. Stopping one call short of the function that
actually computes the value, and then writing arithmetic about it.

leafVisitation at :625 splits each anchor's mass evenly among the leaves beneath it,
accumulates, and reports each leaf as `1 - exp(-a)`. So a saturating transform, not
a division, and every part of my reconstruction fails:

  * mass/leaves is not the formula
  * 2/71 is a loose bound, not a ceiling under saturation, so "a quarter of
    attainable" rested on nothing
  * and your sharpest point: 0.4817/71 = 0.0067845 rounds to 0.0068 while the program
    printed 0.0067. MY RECONSTRUCTION DID NOT REPRODUCE THE NUMBER IT CLAIMED TO
    EXPLAIN, and I did not check that it did. That mismatch was sitting in my own
    arithmetic and I walked past it.

The page now explains the estimand from source and DECLINES TO STATE A CEILING,
because the exact ceiling needs the full posterior over leaves and the full posterior
is not in this console output. It says so in those words. That refusal is the same
move the page spends a whole section praising the library for, two screens further
down, and it should have been my first instinct rather than my third attempt.

PRODUCER LINK: there cannot be one, and the page now says why.
daefa36735a35e21c77675ff85ea0f981bc7b031 is not published -- origin/main is at
7385cf9 with 129 commits unpushed -- so any URL naming that revision would 404. The
Evidence block states that explicitly, gives the full revision for checking in a
local clone, and says plainly that its href is the archived output rather than the
producer. I would rather the page admit an unpublished producer than manufacture a
link that looks authoritative and resolves to nothing.

That is your two blockers. The static figure remains open and unclaimed, and I am
not going to claim it tonight and leave you a third half-thing to review.

Score for the evening, since it is worth writing down: you have now corrected this
one page four times -- unbound output, three false interpretations, false arithmetic,
missing producer identity -- and every correction was specific, reproducible, and
right. The n/a-and-support section is still the only part I have never had to touch.
